Hackathon prototype · 2026

Say So

Learn to actually speak English — out loud.

A virtual classroom where a patient, bilingual AI teacher listens to your voice, corrects you without making you cringe, and drills the exact sounds your first language keeps getting wrong.

Muhammad Kafi Rizki · github.com/kapihimself/say-so

The problem

Most apps teach you to read English.
Nobody teaches you to open your mouth.

Typing is not speaking

Chat-based tutors let learners hide behind a keyboard. The moment they must speak, everything they practised disappears.

Errors are predictable

Indonesian, Spanish and Portuguese speakers don't make random mistakes. They make the same ones: ship/sheep, tin/thin, big→bik.

Shame kills practice

Speaking practice is scarce and embarrassing. Learners need a patient listener who never judges and never gets tired.

The solution

A voice-first classroom that hears you,
knows where you're from, and fixes one thing at a time.

Talk, don't type

Push-to-talk voice input (Whisper) and natural TTS voice out. Every lesson is a conversation you have out loud.

L1-aware teaching

The teacher knows the exact interference rules for Indonesian, Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese speakers — and coaches them by name.

Spoonfed method

Every point follows HOOK → EXPLAIN → SHOW → PRACTICE → CORRECT → REINFORCE → REWARD, graded to your CEFR level A1–C2.

Under the hood

Shipped, tested, and live in a browser.

Stack

Next.js 16 · React 19 · TypeScript · Tailwind v4 · three.js classroom · Supabase (auth + english schema) · zustand · framer-motion.

AI plumbing

Streaming chat completions for the teacher, Whisper-class STT for voice in, OpenAI-compatible TTS for voice out. Every provider is a swappable *_BASE_URL.

Real engineering

A g2p engine + interference rule engine power the Dialect Lens and Mistake Bank. 24 unit tests green: placement engine, g2p, interference rules.

The ask

English isn't a subject.
It's a mouth habit. So say it.

Live demo: open the app, put on headphones, and speak. Next: flashcards with FSRS, a writing coach, roleplay sims, and a progression engine with certificates.
